meridian.note: 第九章 A: inside the 午门 — the walled court behind the iron gate (red walls, glazed coping, giant paving, dry grass in the joints); the 金水河 with its five marble bridges and the bronze lions; the 太和门 with its two files of guards.

props: the 金水河 crossing the court; the five marble bridges are the gaps between its six stretches
the bronze lions before the 太和门
a bronze vat, its rim worn bright

square.note: 第九章 A: the 太和殿 square — an endless paving, the worn stone 御道 down its middle, rows of bronze vats green with age, the three-tiered marble terrace on the north with the sundial and the bronze tortoise.

props: the bronze vats along the square

throne_hall.note: 第九章 A: the 太和殿 — high and dark, gilded pillars wound with dragons (their lacquer gone in places to the red), the floor of dark 金砖 worn to a shine and cracked at the edges, the seven-step dais with the dragon throne, too big for the boy on it.

props: the seven-step dais with the dragon throne

guard_camp.note: 第九章 B: the 大内侍卫营 east of the 午门内 — a square yard of trodden earth, the hacked wooden posts, the weapon racks; 冯策's small duty room north of it, its lamp always lit.

props: the weapon racks, paint gone, blades bright
the desk and the duty book

lanes.note: 第九章 B: the 西长街 — two red walls and a strip of sky, palace lanterns along the coping (paper torn), moss at the walls' foot; its north end wider with cracked vats full of rain, the 养心门 east, the garden gate north. By night the 禁军's lanterns go up and down it.

props: the palace lanterns along the lane (they light whoever stands under them)
cracked vats full of rain by the west wall (something to crouch behind)
the two bronze vats before the 养心门

garden.note: 第九章 B: the 御花园 — Taihu rocks piled on each other with grass in their holes, old cypresses with bark split in strips, a small hall north; the north-west corner's narrow gate, its lock rusted, its hinges oiled. By night the wind in the cypresses covers footsteps; the watch never looks behind the rocks.

props: the Taihu rockery (cover: the watch never looks behind it)
a lantern before the small hall

cold_palace.note: 第九章 B: the 冷宫 — a yard gone to waste, weeds knee-high, saplings in the steps, paper windows half torn, the dry well with its rope grooves and iron rungs bright at the top; 钟嬷嬷's small room north, clean, the unfinished peony on its frame.

props: the embroidery frame with its faded peony

well_tunnel.note: 第九章 B: under the 冷宫's well — wet mud with footprints, iron rungs up; the brick tunnel north, dripping, candle stubs in the joints, a black cord off a 逆灵宫 crown; at its north end steps up to the stone under the 地下密室's bed.

props: a rotten bucket in the mud

yangxin_hall.note: 第九章 C: the 养心殿 — a small swept yard inside the 养心门 (two vats, a crab-apple, a stone stool with a book left open in the dew); the hall, warmer than the 太和殿, the throne and a side table piled with memorials, the vermilion brush dry on the stone; west the 西暖阁 with the kang, the boy's lamp, his father's notes and a map with 岚城？ ringed in red, a window whose latch hangs loose; east the 御书房, shelves of yellow-labelled cases, the desk, the camphor chest sealed 寻剑.

props: the throne on its low dais
the side table piled with memorials
the kang, the lamp and the notes on its table
the camphor chest sealed 寻剑
